target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector. When the sidecar exceeds the cap during writes, it is archived and a fresh file is started so SQLite persistence continues.

## Changes

1. **Bounded reads**: `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses the shared `readRegularFile` helper with an 8 MiB cap instead of unbounded `fs.promises.readFile`.
2. **Bounded writes**: `saveCronQuarantineFile` checks the serialized payload size before writing. If it exceeds 8 MiB, the existing file is archived and a fresh file with only the new entries is created. If a single entry alone exceeds the cap, writes fail with a clear error.
3. **Archive retention**: Archived sidecar files use unique names (`{path}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`). Up to 5 most recent archives are retained; when a new archive pushes the count past 5, the oldest archives are pruned to prevent unbounded disk growth.
4. **Tests**: Regression coverage for bounded reads, oversized write rejection, archive creation and fresh-start recovery, archive pruning at the retention limit.

## User Impact

A corrupted or oversized quarantine sidecar is rejected before OOM. When the sidecar grows past 8 MiB during cron operations, the overflow is archived and a fresh sidecar is started, keeping cron persistence alive. The last 5 overflow archives are preserved for review; older ones are pruned.

## Evidence

AI-assisted implementation; maintainer-reviewed and validated.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users could silently lose inbound agent activities when the process stopped after Bot Framework received a webhook but before detached processing adopted the turn. The webhook returned success without durable admission, so Bot Framework had no reason to retry; severity was HIGH because the loss was silent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Microsoft Teams now adopts the shared durable channel-ingress drain. Dispatchable activities use `activity.id` as the event ID, matching the `@microsoft/teams.api` contract that it uniquely identifies an activity on the channel, and `conversation.id` as the serialization lane. The webhook acknowledgement waits for durable append, while downstream work uses deferred claims and merged-debounce fan-out adoption following the proven Signal pattern.

The adapter journals message turns and adaptive-card agent turns only. `messageUpdate`, poll votes, file consent, reactions, and other dedicated non-agent workflows remain outside the ingress journal.

Landing review also fixed live-context payload substitution, an install/append race and leak, duplicate `next()` invocation, stale context after failed append, and the test seam renamed when `main` retired the settled dispatcher.

## User Impact

Accepted Microsoft Teams agent activities survive process interruption and replay after restart instead of disappearing after an early webhook acknowledgement. Conversation ordering remains serialized, debounced turns settle every constituent claim, and non-agent Teams workflows retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Post-rebase full Microsoft Teams suite: 1,113 tests passed, including the loopback lifecycle tests that an earlier sandbox could not run.
- Dedicated durability proof: 14-case ingress matrix plus 3 lifecycle tests covering deferred claims, merged fan-out adoption, and gated no-dispatch completion.
- Current exact-head changed-surface rerun: 39 tests passed across `msteams-ingress`, message-handler ingress lifecycle, monitor lifecycle, and adaptive-card handling.
- Hard-zero gates: `node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mjs` and `node scripts/check-deadcode-unused-files.mjs` both reported zero entries; `git diff --check` passed.
- The original autoreview build-stage attempt was blocked by sandbox networking. Manual review found and drove the on-branch context, lifecycle, and dispatcher-seam fixes listed above; all prior findings were adjudicated and resolved.

target.title: fix(browser): time out download saves
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser download waits used the configured timeout only until Playwright emitted the download event. After that event, the timer was cleared before `download.saveAs(...)` ran, so a stalled save could leave the browser tool call hanging indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download capture now removes the event listener when the download is observed, but keeps the original deadline active until the save operation settles. If the save hangs, the same timeout rejects the tool call instead of waiting forever.

## User Impact

Browser download tools now fail with the configured timeout when the browser starts a download but Playwright cannot finish saving it, making stalled downloads recoverable for agents and users.

target.title: fix(channels): prevent observe-only delivery and orphaned turn adoption
target.body:
Related: #110095

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two latent turn-kernel failures for durable channel ingress. A prepared turn could accept a top-level adoption lifecycle without ever completing it, allowing the ingress watchdog to time out and redeliver. A direct SDK call to assembled-turn dispatch could also execute a real transport delivery despite observe-only admission while reporting that nothing was dispatched.

This is a hardening follow-up to merged PR #110095 (`601ffa253037`), which moved inbound turn execution into core. No live affected adapters are known today.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared dispatchers already own their reply options, so the kernel now rejects the invalid top-level lifecycle combination instead of silently dropping it. Observe-only delivery suppression now lives in the assembled-turn lifecycle owner, beside result masking, so both kernel-routed and direct SDK entry points share the same behavior. The plugin runtime mock mirrors both contracts.

The patch stays additive and bounded: no public type shape changes, no ingress policy changes, and no transport-specific behavior.

## User Impact

Durable-ingress adapters get fail-fast protection against orphaned turn adoption, and direct SDK assembled-turn dispatch cannot leak observe-only replies to a real channel. Existing valid turn plans keep their current behavior. No changelog entry: latent internal hardening with no known live victims.

target.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A user running a schema-11 agent DB (main/dev build) had the updater stop their healthy gateway and install v2026.7.2-beta.2, which supports schema 9. Every subsequent health/connect/message retry then ran a full synchronous `quick_check` + `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check` over the 21 GB database on the gateway main thread (30-45s, 100% CPU), only to fail with "schema 11 > 9" - and nothing latched the failure, so the scan repeated forever. Three separate gaps stacked: the updater has no DB-schema preflight, the expensive integrity scan ran before the cheap version gate (#105179 ordering), and terminal open failures were retried from scratch.

Discussion context: Discord report by Dave Morin, sanity-checked against `main`; the integrity-on-open series (#104938, #105179, #105222, #106065, #108663) is a defensive response to the still-open corruption incident #101290 (broken `schema_meta` index).

## Why This Change Was Made

Downgrades must be refused instantly and cheaply at every layer, upgrades must stay proven and communicated, and full-file integrity scanning belongs off the hot path while keeping the detection #101290 still needs:

- **Cheap gates first**: both open paths now check `user_version` + schema owner before any scan. A newer-schema DB refuses in microseconds with an error naming the build that owns the DB (`schema_meta.app_version` is now stamped, previously always `null`) and linking the new docs page.
- **Scan rescoped**: steady-state opens verify only `integrity_check('schema_meta')` - the observed #101290/#105179 corruption class - plus the redundant `quick_check` pass is gone everywhere (`integrity_check` is a strict superset per sqlite.org/pragma.html). The full scan still runs where slow is correct: before a pending migration (now with a user-visible log line), in doctor/backup/compact, and in a new gateway background verifier.
- **Background verifier**: worker thread, first run 5 min after boot then daily, serial full `integrity_check` + `foreign_key_check` per DB, results persisted to a new additive `database_verifications` table in the state DB. On proven corruption it quarantines the DB: closes any live handle and latches the path so later opens fail fast until doctor repairs it.
- **Terminal-failure latch**: newer-schema and corruption failures latch per path (process-local); retries no longer rescan. Transient errors (BUSY, permissions) never latch. Doctor repair paths clear the latch.
- **Gateway boot preflight**: header-only version sweep of the state DB + registered agent DBs; refuses startup with one structured error per incompatible DB.
- **Updater preflight**: `package.json` now publishes `openclaw.schemaVersions`; `openclaw update` fetches the target's declared support (npm registry / git `show <rev>:package.json`) and refuses before stopping any service when an on-disk DB is newer than the target supports. Dry-run reports it; targets without metadata skip the check.
- **No new downgrade cliff**: deliberately no schema version bumps in this PR. The `database_verifications` table is additive derived cache (same fold pattern as 0c17cd4f1f2), so older builds still open the state DB.
- **Docs**: new `https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas` - layout, versioning contract, per-version history mapped to release tags, integrity-check matrix, and an explicitly unsupported manual downgrade recipe with a worked 11->9 example.

## User Impact

- Beta upgraders from older releases: unchanged proven forward migrations (fixtures at schema 1/7/9/10 all land on current), now with a clear "migration pending, verifying integrity first" log instead of a silent multi-second stall on large DBs.
- Downgrade attempts: refused before the service is stopped (updater), at gateway boot (preflight), and at every open (version gate) - each refusal instant, actionable, and pointing at the docs page.
- Steady-state performance: per-open validation on a 756 MB DB drops from 763 ms to 1.6 ms (measured, ~475x); on the reported 21 GB DB that is ~30-45 s -> ~2 ms per open, and CLI one-shots stop paying a full-file scan per process launch.
- Corruption detection moves off-thread but stays daily and still fails closed before mutations via the schema_meta check, migration-time full scan, and quarantine latch.

## Evidence

- Focused suites (all green, single run): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-integrity.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-user-version.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-maintenance.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.test.ts src/state/openclaw-database-verify.test.ts src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-sqlite-compact.test.ts src/commands/doctor.test.ts src/infra/update-check.test.ts src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.test.ts src/infra/tsdown-config.test.ts test/release-check.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.test.ts`
- Contract coverage: newer+corrupt DB fails with `SqliteSchemaVersionError` (no scan), latch fail-fast + clear-on-repair, quarantine closes a live handle, boot preflight fixtures, updater refusal before service stop (package + git modes, dry-run, missing-metadata skip), package.json/constants drift guard, worker bundle packaging guard.
- Perf: synthetic 756 MB agent DB - old per-open cost 763.2 ms (quick 171.4 + integrity 591.6 + fk 0.2) vs new 1.6 ms (schema_meta check 0.9 + version gate 0.7).
- `node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify` clean; `git diff --check` clean; oxfmt clean on all changed files; docs MDX/link checks green (738 files, 6061 links).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (local fallback; Blacksmith backend timed out): all lanes green except the pre-existing main `check:test-types` orphans noted below; core `pnpm tsgo` clean, import cycles 0.
- Six structured autoreview rounds (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): every accepted finding fixed (durable quarantine rows enforced at open, preflight indeterminate fail-closed in the updater, post-stop TOCTOU recheck, git-metadata unreadable refusal, exact-version install pinning, doctor clear-failure surfacing). One consciously rejected finding remains, documented in code comments: when persisting a quarantine row fails (after a bounded retry of terminal rows), the quarantine stays process-local until the next daily verifier pass; the proposed durable out-of-band marker is a new storage surface (dedicated quarantine store) that needs a maintainer decision - flagged as follow-up.
- Post-rebase note: `check:test-types` is broken on current `origin/main` by two orphaned test files (`src/shared/deferred-event-buffer.test.ts`, `src/tools/protocol.test.ts`) whose prod modules were deleted by the deadcode refactors; unrelated to this PR and repaired separately on main.

target.title: fix(ci): persist warm runtime caches across runs
target.body:
Related: #110298

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where CI cache writers reported successful Blacksmith sticky-disk commits, but later jobs repeatedly restored the original dependency, Vitest transform, and Node compile snapshots. The dependency store therefore repeated a 12.6 GB prune, and identical Vitest generations were cleared on every run instead of producing warm-cache gains.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime transform and compile caches now use immutable upstream Actions cache archives, which Blacksmith transparently accelerates. CI shards are restore-only; the daily or explicitly dispatched warmer is the sole test-cache writer, while build compile archives rotate at most once per UTC day.

The multi-GiB dependency tree remains on one O(1) sticky-disk family. Canonical main preflight is its sole serialized writer and 8 GiB maintenance owner, the key rotates from v4 to v5, and every consumer keeps the exact fingerprint fallback because [upstream stickydisk issue #54](https://github.com/useblacksmith/stickydisk/issues/54) documents delayed snapshot visibility even between dependent jobs. The stickydisk action pin also includes upstream's hot-attach zero-size fix.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Pull requests and main CI can restore warm transform and bytecode seeds without concurrent filesystem writers or per-PR sticky-disk growth. Old immutable Actions archives are bounded by normal LRU and inactivity eviction; only one live dependency sticky family remains.

## Evidence

- Before: dependency writer runs 29626241027 and later repeatedly committed fingerprint 75197f, but subsequent eu-west/X64 mounts still restored 73f052. Warmer 29627216071 pruned 69,431 files / 12.6 GB / 1,417 packages; later warmers repeated the identical prune.
- Before: identical Vitest generation f0d7e5 was cleared on every sampled run from 02:08 through 02:47 despite successful approximately 325 MB commit logs.
- Upstream contract checked: useblacksmith/stickydisk issue #54; PR #58 documents read-only parallel clones; commit 6d373c96 fixes hot-attach zero-size formatting races. Upstream useblacksmith/cache recommends the maintained actions/cache action because Blacksmith accelerates it transparently.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 82 passed, 1 platform skip.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` — zizmor and composite interpolation guards passed.
- `node scripts/docs-list.js` — passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Fresh branch autoreview — no accepted/actionable findings.

Post-land proof will dispatch the warmer once, verify a later Actions cache restore, verify a later main run restores the v5 dependency fingerprint, then delete only the four exact retired eu-west/amd64 v4/v2 identities.

Closes #110340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a CLI-backed agent could see a misleading combined timeout warning after the overall turn limit expired, while active CLI work could be replayed automatically and duplicate partial side effects.

The observed production case had a stored 600-second agent timeout. Claude CLI was still draining internal background work when the parent process was terminated; OpenClaw retried the turn, then showed advice that conflated the overall timeout with the no-output watchdog.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI timeout failures now carry structured mode, duration, activity, active-tool, and background-task context. CLI tool/output phases participate in the existing replay-safety boundary, and transient retries now respect that boundary. User-facing copy distinguishes overall and no-output limits, reports stopped work and partial-effect risk, states when automatic replay was suppressed, and gives mode-specific remediation.

Documentation now explains the normal 48-hour Gateway default, the separate `openclaw agent` 600-second request fallback, CLI watchdog profiles, the 12-hour configuration example, and why detached OpenClaw sub-agents are the durable choice for long work.

## User Impact

Operators can tell which limit fired and change only the relevant setting. Active turns are not automatically replayed after tool execution or assistant output begins. CLI-internal background work is identified as sharing the parent process, while detached OpenClaw sub-agents remain no-timeout by default.

Release note: Fixed CLI timeout handling so active work is not replayed, warnings identify the correct timeout and stopped work, and long-running task guidance is explicit.

## Evidence

- Live incident reconstruction: two consecutive 600-second `claude-cli` terminations on OpenClaw 2026.7.2; the first turn was automatically replayed while CLI background work was active. Gateway health remained normal.

target.title: fix(outbound): keep newline-mode paragraphs as separate outbound units
target.body:
Fixes #109032

## User-facing bug

With `chunkMode: "newline"` configured, automatic visible replies from the Codex agent runtime can collapse multiple intended paragraphs into a single WhatsApp bubble, while the OpenClaw runtime delivers the same response shape as separate bubbles under identical channel configuration.

## Root cause

`chunkByParagraph` (src/auto-reply/chunk.ts) splits on blank-line boundaries but then **packs adjacent paragraphs back into one chunk whenever they fit under the transport limit**. The OpenClaw runtime path streams block-by-block — the planner sees one block per call, so packing never has two blocks to join. The Codex runtime hands `planOutboundTextMessageUnits` (src/infra/outbound/message-plan.ts) the full reply text in one call, so its blank-line-separated paragraphs get packed into one outbound unit → one bubble.

The transport-size limit was doing double duty as a packing target. Newline mode's paragraph boundaries encode the author's visible-reply boundaries; a limit should only *split* oversized payloads, never *join* logical blocks (exactly as the issue states).

## Fix

- `chunkByParagraph` gains a `packAdjacent` option (default `true` — every existing caller keeps current behavior).
- `chunkMarkdownTextWithMode` forwards the option for the markdown path.
- The outbound planner's `newline` branch — the one place where logical block boundaries must survive — passes `packAdjacent: false` for both text and markdown chunker paths.

Length-splitting of oversized single paragraphs is unchanged, fence handling is unchanged, and all other chunker consumers (Slack/Telegram/Matrix/Feishu/Mattermost/plugin-sdk streaming paths) are unaffected by default.

Two existing `deliver.test.ts` expectations pinned the old packing behavior ("Line one\n\nLine two" → 1 send; "Alpha\n\nBeta" packed); they are updated to the issue-expected behavior with comments referencing #109032.

## Targeted tests

- `chunk.test.ts`: `packAdjacent: false` keeps paragraphs separate; still length-splits an oversized paragraph; does not join across fence-preserved boundaries.
- `message-plan.test.ts`: two blank-line paragraphs → two units, for both text and markdown chunker modes.
- `deliver.test.ts`: end-to-end `deliverOutboundPayloads` produces one send per paragraph in newline mode.

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix: stop node alerts replaying after Gateway restart
target.body:
Closes #110354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with multiple paired nodes would receive a macOS "Node connected" alert for every existing node after a Gateway restart or fleet reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

After `hello-ok` and the ready transition, the Gateway now atomically classifies the authenticated node's canonical pairing record as a first connection or reconnect while persisting its monotonic connection timestamp. Only the first successful connection can create an alert. A replacement session for the same authenticated node can take over that pending alert; ordinary reconnects remain silent.

This removes the process-local five-minute reconnect cooldown. Durable pairing metadata now owns the one-time decision, so restarting the Gateway cannot replay the fleet.

## User Impact

Connecting a newly approved node still produces one routed macOS notification. Already-paired nodes reconnecting later, including after a Gateway restart, no longer produce misleading "new node" notification storms.

## Evidence

- Redacted before-fix live status: five paired nodes reconnected within 7.431 seconds (four macOS, one Linux). All four Macs supported notifications, none reported recent Accessibility activity, so each source handshake entered fallback fanout.
- Focused local proof: 64 tests passed across `src/infra/node-pairing.test.ts`, `src/gateway/node-connection-notifications.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.node-version-mismatch.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxsmvxs0gtwe6c3616tamh5x`: `pnpm check:changed` passed core and core-test typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, plugin boundaries, pairing guards, database-first guards, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh autoreview completed with no accepted or actionable findings after concurrency, identity, and handshake-lifecycle review.
- Pairing identity contract: authenticated node pairing is keyed by the canonical device ID in `prepareGatewayNodeConnect` and `beginNodePairingConnect`. `src/infra/node-pairing-migration.ts` folds a legacy row only when its ID matches a node-role device record and removes orphan legacy aliases. The removed `client.instanceId` metadata write predated that security/canonicalization path; current docs describe `--node-id` as a legacy client instance ID that does not reset pairing. No shipped pairing record requires the removed alias write.
- Upgrade regression proof: `src/infra/node-pairing-migration.test.ts` now seeds a retired client-instance alias beside its canonical device identity, proves migration drops the orphan alias, reapproves the canonical node surface, and proves the canonical device claims exactly one first connection followed by a silent reconnect. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxsrdbjqfpxew35mn7apfech` passed the focused suite (4/4); final autoreview was clean at 0.94 correctness.
- Native two-Mac after-fix proof was not available without installing the patched Gateway and introducing a disposable newly paired node. The durable claim, concurrent-handshake, replacement-session, disconnect-cancel, and restart-relevant paths are covered deterministically.

## Release Note

Mac node connection alerts now appear only for a node's first successful connection; reconnects and Gateway restarts no longer replay alerts for previously paired nodes.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip                  (pass)
 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real Nostr relay was not executed (no relay credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(memory-embeddings): use longer backoff for rate-limit (429) errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw memory index` encounters a rate-limit (429) error from the embedding provider, the retry loop uses the normal 500ms base delay with an 8000ms cap. Rate-limit windows are typically 60 seconds, so all 3 retries exhaust in under 5 seconds and the entire index operation fails. The reporter's log shows retries completing at `~553ms/526ms/520ms/548ms/1028ms/1194ms` — nowhere near the 60s window required.

## Changes

- **New `isRateLimitMemoryEmbeddingError()` in policy** — separately detects 429 / `resource has been exhausted` errors vs general transient errors (5xx, network blips)
- **`rateLimitBaseDelayMs` (30s) param on `runMemoryEmbeddingRetryLoop`** — when a rate-limit error fires, use this base instead of the normal `500ms`; produces wait sequence: 30s → 60s → 120s
- **`rateLimitMaxDelayMs` (120s) in `waitForEmbeddingRetry`** — used when the computed delay already exceeds the normal 8s cap, so the longer rate-limit delay isn't clamped away
- **Threaded through `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit`** — both retry loops and recursive split calls get the same longer backoff for rate-limit errors
- Normal transient errors (connection reset, fetch failed, timed out, 5xx) still use the original 500ms base — no regression

## Evidence

- All 18 existing tests pass (including the 3 new rate-limit backoff tests)
- New test `uses longer backoff for rate-limit errors when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: 429 error with default config produces waits = [30000, 60000] before exhausting 3 attempts
- New test `still uses short backoff for non-rate-limit retryable errors even when rateLimitBaseDelayMs is set` confirms: transient `fetch failed` with the same config still uses [500ms] delay — no cross-contamination
- The `waitForEmbeddingRetry` max-delay detection is implicit: if `delayMs > 8000` (the normal cap), the code picks the rate-limit cap; otherwise the normal 8s cap

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving background-generated media could see the same attachment posted multiple times after one successful generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The duplicate was not caused by the handoff retry ladder itself. Restart-safe delivery preserved the model's `MEDIA:` directive and then appended the same host-owned attachment as a second payload, while the completion prompt could separately tell the requester session to resend it.

target.title: fix(config): compaction.enabled field rejected by config schema despite being read by the runtime
target.body:
Closes #110065

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could not disable auto-compaction through configuration. The session runtime reads `compaction.enabled` to control auto-compaction on/off (`settings-manager.ts:667`: `this.settings.compaction?.enabled ?? true`), but both the config schema's Zod `.strict()` object and the `AgentCompactionConfig` TypeScript type omitted the `enabled` field. Setting `enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` caused the entire config to be rejected as invalid with `agents.defaults.compaction: Invalid input`.

Users experiencing premature compaction had no `enabled: false` workaround while waiting for underlying usage-accounting fixes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `enabled: z.boolean().optional()` to the compaction Zod schema and the `enabled?: boolean` property to the `AgentCompactionConfig` TS type — matching the runtime's existing `?? true` default. The field is optional: absent means enabled (the existing default), `false` disables auto-compaction entirely as the settings manager intended. The schema stays `.strict()` so truly unknown fields are still rejected. A new schema help entry documents the field.

## User Impact

Users can now set `compaction.enabled: false` in `openclaw.json` (or via `openclaw config set`) to disable automatic context compaction. Absent configurations behave exactly as before (`enabled` defaults to true).

## Evidence

### Real runtime behavior proof (production Zod AgentDefaultsSchema)

Loading the production `AgentDefaultsSchema` (the same Zod schema used by `openclaw validate`, `openclaw status`, and every config-load path) with `compaction.enabled: false`:

```
[proof] enabled=false accepted by real Zod schema: true
[proof] unknown field rejected (strictness preserved): true
[proof] full compaction config with enabled=false accepted: true
[proof] Zod parse output: {"compaction":{"enabled":false}}
[proof] ON MAIN: this same Zod.safeParse call returns success=false -- config rejected as invalid
[proof] PROOF COMPLETE -- production AgentDefaultsSchema now accepts compaction.enabled
```

The `.strict()` guard still fires for truly unknown keys -- the schema accepts exactly the field the runtime reads and nothing else.

### Schema validation regression (real `validateConfigObject`)

- `validateConfigObject({ agents: { defaults: { compaction: { enabled: false } } } })` -- passes with the fix; fails against unfixed `main` (the `.strict()` schema rejects `enabled` as an unrecognized key).
- `validateConfigObject({ agents: { defaults: { compaction: { nonexistentField: true } } } })` -- still fails in both states, proving the `.strict()` guard stays intact.

### Unit regression coverage

- `config.compaction-settings.test.ts`: 7 tests pass (2 new: compaction.enabled toggle accepted; absent defaults to undefined for runtime `?? true`).
- `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`: 36 tests pass (2 new, including the strictness-preservation test).
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` -- passed (no type errors).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on both test files -- 43 passed.
- Scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` pass on the five changed files.

### Unrelated CI failures

`checks-node-compact-small-5` and `checks-node-compact-small-6` fail in `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts` ("Apple catalog apps/ios/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings is stale") -- an iOS localization catalog staleness issue on `main` unrelated to this PR's config schema change.

`check-test-types` was fixed in a21f752 by adding `enabled` to the `AgentCompactionConfig` TS type.

target.title: fix(gateway): preserve restart intent across coalesced config writes
target.body:
Closes #105623

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway config reloader coalesces writes that arrive while an earlier write is still being applied. The pending slot correctly keeps the newest config payload, but it also replaced the entire `afterWrite` intent.

That creates a reliability gap for this sequence:

1. write A is being applied;
2. committed write B arrives and requires a process restart;
3. write C arrives before A finishes, contains the newest config, and does not independently require a restart.

Before this change, C replaced B in the pending slot and erased B's restart requirement. The reloader then applied C without restarting, even though one of the committed, not-yet-applied writes had already established that the running gateway could not safely converge through hot reload alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change gives the coalesced pending state two intentionally different merge rules:

- config data, hashes, prepared candidates, and refresh metadata still use the newest write;
- an unapplied `restart` intent is retained until the pending state is processed, unless the newer write also supplies its own restart intent.

The scope is deliberately limited to the in-process pending slot. It does not change config schemas, debounce behavior, watcher lifecycle, hot-reload planning, or restart handling after processing begins.

An existing regression test already proves that a restart intent from an obsolete **active** write must not leak into a newer pending write. The new test covers the complementary invariant: a restart intent from an unapplied **pending** committed write must not be erased by a later coalesced non-restart write.

## User Impact

Rapid successive config writes no longer leave the gateway running with stale process state when an intermediate committed write required a restart. The latest config still wins, and ordinary `none`/`auto` behavior is unchanged when no pending restart exists.

## Tests

Added a deterministic three-write regression test that blocks write A during plugin-record loading, queues restart-requiring write B, then coalesces newer write C. It verifies that:

- exactly one restart occurs;
- the restart reason comes from B;
- the restarted gateway receives C's newest config;
- no hot reload is performed instead.

## Evidence

- Red test before the production change: the new focused case failed in all three gateway projects because `onRestart` was called 0 times instead of 1.
- Green focused test after the change: 3 passed, 402 skipped.
- Full affected test file after the change: 405 passed.
- Post-rebase validation on Node 24.15.0: `pnpm test src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` — 135/135 passed.
- Post-rebase changed-file gate: `CI=1 pnpm check:changed -- src/gateway/config-reload.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` — passed all `core` and `coreTests` checks, including formatting, typechecks, lint, import cycles, and repository guards.
- Pre-rebase full gates on the same two-file patch: `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` — passed.
- Ready-for-review GitHub CI completed with 73 passing checks. The only functional failure was `checks-node-compact-small-5`, where two unrelated Apple localization tests report a stale `apps/ios/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`; `openclaw/ci-gate` consequently failed as the aggregate gate. The exact base commit fails in the same job on `main` ([main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29629284704)), and focused upstream fixes are already open in [#110370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110370), [#110387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110387), and [#110388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110388). No failure referenced the two gateway files changed here.
- A repo-wide local `pnpm test` run was also attempted on macOS. It is not reported as a green signal because unrelated platform/environment failures occurred (`/var` vs `/private/var`, Bash 3.2 incompatibilities, unavailable loopback aliases/incomplete optional workspace dependencies), and the iMessage extension shard stopped making progress. The affected gateway tests above remained green; clean GitHub CI is the authoritative full-run gate for this PR.
- Affected-test timing check: baseline `config-reload.test.ts` ran 402 tests in 5.59s; the patched file ran 405 tests in 4.77s. These timings are included only as a regression check, not as a performance claim.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed the relevant reloader state transitions, neighboring tests, and final diff, and ran the validation commands documented above.

target.title: fix: readability extraction handles raw-text pseudo tags
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users fetching readable HTML pages could lose Readability extraction when the page embeds large client-side templates or style/script text containing strings such as repeated `<div>` tags.

The user-realistic path is:

```text
web_fetch -> runWebFetch(text/html) -> extractReadableContent -> web-readability extractor -> sanitizeHtml -> exceedsEstimatedHtmlNestingDepth -> Readability result or fallback
```

Before this fix, the nesting preflight scanned raw HTML text inside elements such as `<script>` and could count pseudo tags in JavaScript/CSS/template text as real DOM nesting. On an otherwise readable article, that made the extractor return `null`, so `web_fetch` could fall back to provider/basic HTML extraction instead of returning the higher-quality Readability result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The web-readability nesting preflight now treats the targeted raw-text/RCDATA and legacy raw-text-like element contents as text while preserving the existing depth guard for real markup outside those elements. It still counts the element itself and still enforces the maximum nesting depth for the rest of the document.

The start-tag scan is quote-aware but remains bounded. A quoted attribute value like `data-close="</script>"` cannot make the preflight resume scanning inside a raw-text start tag, malformed apparent tags cannot trigger an unbounded scan, and valid long start tags are still counted conservatively when their delimiter is beyond the bounded scan window. This PR does not change fetch behavior, provider fallback behavior, SSRF/network policy, the 1 MB readability limit, or the general Readability parser.

## User Impact

`web_fetch` keeps readable article extraction quality on modern pages that include embedded JavaScript, CSS, or legacy fallback/template text containing HTML-like content. Pages that are genuinely too deeply nested still hit the same safety guard, and malformed fetched HTML remains bounded during the preflight.

## Evidence

User-realistic proof:

- Entry point checked: `web_fetch` on `text/html` content with the default readable extraction path.
- Before-fix runtime probe on upstream `main`: an otherwise readable article with `"<div>".repeat(3101)` inside `<script>` returned `{ "hasResult": false, "title": null, "textStart": null }`.
- After-fix runtime probe with the same pseudo-tag payload plus a quoted raw-text attribute boundary returned:

```json
{"hasResult":true,"title":"Example Article","textStart":"Main content starts here wit"}
```

Reviewer-feedback proof added after ClawSweeper review:

```text
noembed  {"hasResult":true,"title":"Example Article","textStart":"Main content starts here wit"}
noframes {"hasResult":true,"title":"Example Article","textStart":"Main content starts here wit"}
```

The legacy raw-text probe uses repeated apparent tags inside `<noembed>...</noembed>` and `<noframes>...</noframes>` content. A malformed apparent-tag flood probe with `"<a".repeat(50000)` completed and returned the expected fallback signal:

```json
{"result":null,"elapsedMs":11}
```

For the long-valid-tag review case, the preflight rejects 3,101 valid opening tags whose attributes push `>` beyond the bounded scan window:

```json
{"longTagRejected":true,"elapsedMs":3,"length":697725}
```

Focused validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/web-readability/web-content-extractor.test.ts` - passed, 1 file / 8 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/web-readability/web-content-extractor.ts extensions/web-readability/web-content-extractor.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

Additional checks:

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` still fails locally in untouched `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` with existing errors around `BlockedIpv6Range` values `"benchmarking"`, `"orchid2"`, and a union callable at line 367. Remote `check-prod-types` has passed on the earlier heads; remote CI is the source of truth for the updated head.

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets only when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases. Status-only post-download finalization gets **one non-renewable grace arm**; further status-only lines (including distinct novel freeform statuses) cannot renew it, so:
- non-advancing drips fail closed
- advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime
- healthy finite finalization phases survive inside one grace window
- cycling or novel status drips without completed progress cannot act as an unlimited keepalive

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping /api/pull stream fails closed with a no-progress error. Healthy pulls that keep advancing completed survive. Finite status-only finalization survives within one grace budget. Distinct novel status drips without completed progress are bounded — removing the prior availability hang bypass.

## Evidence

Exact head: `6b2f322c48e`

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Ollama setup `/api/pull` no longer hangs when status-only NDJSON drips without advancing `completed` (including distinct novel status strings).
- Real environment tested: local Node function tests via Vitest fake timers against `ensureOllamaModelPulled` (mocked fetch streams).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

target.title: fix(cron): stop a cron job's own marker from blocking its awaited wake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `wakeMode: "now"` main-session cron job installs its active execution marker before awaiting `runHeartbeatOnce`. The heartbeat admission guard then sees cron work in progress and can reject the wake that the job itself owns. The cron path falls back to an asynchronous request and records success before delivery is confirmed.

This is a deterministic defect found while investigating #105257. It fixes an adjacent, reproducible self-block; it does not claim to close that broader intermittent report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron path now passes its exact active marker `{ jobId, token }` through the internal Gateway heartbeat adapter. The heartbeat runner bypasses only that still-current marker:

- another cron job still blocks the wake;
- a same-ID replacement marker still blocks the stale owner;
- an absent or stale owner keeps the previous busy behavior;
- queued `cron.run` work cannot deadlock on its own `CommandLane.Cron` entry;
- the public plugin heartbeat facade cannot supply or forge internal ownership.

The exact token matters. Discounting by job ID alone would allow a superseded execution to claim ownership of a newer run.

## User Impact

Main-session `wakeMode: "now"` cron runs now wait for their owned heartbeat delivery before recording terminal success. Other cron work continues to enforce the existing admission fence. No config, storage, protocol, or public plugin API changes.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage exercises the full decision surface:

- exact marker, unrelated marker, same-ID replacement, and stale replacement;
- direct manual run, Gateway-queued `cron.run`, and natural scheduled firing;
- real heartbeat runner integration and Gateway adapter forwarding;
- owned Cron-lane pressure versus unowned busy behavior;
- marker and command-lane cleanup before sandbox deletion.

Results:

- 88 focused tests passed across cron active jobs, timer/service, Gateway adapter, and heartbeat runner.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on Blacksmith Testbox ([run 29629429145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29629429145)).
- Fresh autoreview found no actionable issue.

Live proof used the official OpenAI API with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, an isolated QA state root, and a custom loopback Gateway port (`41103`):

- Natural timer: outbound delivery `1784347997662`, terminal success `1784347997665`.

commands.author: xydigit-zt

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip                  (pass)
 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real Nostr relay was not executed (no relay credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

_Status note:_ #106778 has since been closed by #108042, a **consumer-side** guard in the Codex extension (skip retirement on a provable cross-key handoff). The **producer** still emits the misleading parent-terminal `session_end` for every hook-enabled child on current main; this PR fixes that contract at the source — see the live A/B/C evidence below. The two are complementary.


## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.
- **Main reset-in-place** emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier; a dashboard session is replaced via `sessions.reset` (which retires its binding in place), never a create-succession.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

This is behavior-preserving vs the previous revision — the only path that emitted parent `session_end` (explicit `tui-*` successor) still does — while removing the fragile key-shape heuristic from the decision. Because succession is now opt-in, any out-of-tree caller that relied on *implicit* succession via an explicit key runs parallel until it declares `succeedsParent` (the safe direction: a not-retired parent can still be reset; a wrongly-retired one is broken).

**Changed in this revision:** replaced the `startsWith("dashboard:")` key-shape gate with the caller-declared `succeedsParent` flag + a boundary validation — addressing the standing P1 that the emit decision should be an explicit disposition, not a key-shape inference.

**Maintainer note.** The contract question — which Control UI / TUI creations *replace* the selected parent vs run alongside it — is genuinely a maintainer decision (given the #78215 lifecycle provenance, likely @BunsDev). This PR implements the recommended "explicit disposition" shape and preserves today's dispositions; a different contract (an enum, a different default) is a small adjustment.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

### Live Codex-backed A/B/C run (real standalone gateway + codex app-server 0.144.4 + real model turns)

A single run per tree, same harness on three trees (Ubuntu VPS, Node v24.18.0): an **ephemeral standalone gateway** (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --bind loopback --auth token`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/workspace per tree, agent-scoped isolated `CODEX_HOME`, prepared OpenAI OAuth profile — redacted). Parent = the agent main session (`agent:main:main`). Turns are real `gpt-5.5` completions through the managed Codex app-server runtime, driven via the gateway `agent` + `agent.wait` RPC. Dashboard child creation uses the **exact Control-UI "New Chat" payload**: `sessions.create {parentSessionKey, emitCommandHooks:true}` (key omitted → the gateway mints `agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>`). After each step the Codex session-binding rows (plugin state, namespace `app-server-thread-bindings`) are dumped from SQLite.

**Built-in emission detector.** This PR's tree does **not** contain #108042 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms), so its Codex consumer is the old handler that retires the binding on **any** terminal parent `session_end` — and the rollover step below proves that detector live (the binding *is* retired when the event fires). Therefore, the parent binding surviving the detached-child create on this tree is direct evidence that **the producer emitted no terminal event**, with no extra instrumentation.

| Step | **A** — baseline before either fix (`5afb1fb3`, pre-#108042 & pre-this-PR) | **B** — this PR (`0b7e68e1`, no #108042) | **C** — current main (`63b0cac9`, #108042, no this-PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent turn 1 | ✅ ok — binding `{"state":"active","threadId":…}` | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| Create dashboard child (New-Chat payload) | 💥 **parent binding tombstoned**: `{"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}` | ✅ binding **intact** (`active`, same threadId) | ✅ binding intact |
| Parent turn 2 | 💥 **fails at the durable generation fence**: `Codex session generation is no longer current: <sessionId>` | ✅ **ok — the original parent still works** | ✅ ok |
| Turn in a fresh session | ✅ ok (new sessions work while the parent stays broken — matches the failure #106778 reports) | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| `sessions.create {key:"tui-…", succeedsParent:true}` | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` (contract is new in this PR) | ✅ accepted — **parent binding retired (genuine rollover)**; a real turn in the successor session (`sessionKey agent:main:tui-e2e-rollover`) then completes | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` |

**Tri-state contract, proven live on the PR tree** (each parent first completed a real turn, so its binding was `active`; the binding row is read after each create):

| `succeedsParent` on an explicit non-dashboard successor key | Parent binding after create | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | opt-in rollover |
| **omitted** | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | **legacy rollover preserved** (the P1 compatibility contract) |
| `false` | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | opt-out, parallel |
| omitted, minted **dashboard** child | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | detached by construction — the #106778 path |

A follow-up turn on a genuinely succeeded predecessor fails at the generation fence, as it should — retirement semantics for real successions are unchanged.

- **A reproduces the persisted-state failure #106778 reports, live**: a *successful* detached-dashboard-child create writes a tombstone of the same shape and under the same binding key the issue documents (`entry_key: session-key:main:…`, `value_json {"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}`), and the next parent turn fails permanently at the equivalent durable-generation fence in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts` while new sessions keep working. (The fence message wording evolved between versions; the issue's build printed "binding generation was retired".)
- **B (this PR) proves both requested paths live**: the parent keeps completing real Codex-backed turns after the detached child is created (producer emits no terminal event — see the built-in detector above), and an explicit `succeedsParent` successor still rolls the parent over, with a real turn completing in the successor session.
- **C (current main)**: the parent binding also survives detached-child creation — #108042's consumer-side guard protects the Codex plugin today. The producer path in `session-create-service.ts` is unchanged between A and C (git history), and tree A demonstrates live what that producer emission does to a pre-guard consumer; any other plugin that treats the parent-terminal hook as terminal remains exposed on main. Because `succeedsParent` does not exist on main, a *genuine* succession also cannot be declared. The two fixes are complementary: #108042 hardens the Codex consumer; this PR fixes the lifecycle contract at the source.


### Persisted-state consequence — proven in-boundary over a real store

The destructive step lives in the Codex extension, and its bundled suite already asserts it over a **real** `createCodexAppServerBindingStore`: `session_end(reason:"new")` retires the generation (`read() → undefined` — the `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` tombstone #106778 reports), while non-terminal reasons (`shutdown`, `restart`, `compaction`) leave it intact. So the persisted mutation is real and reason-selective — suppressing the parent `session_end` for a parallel child is exactly what keeps the binding alive.

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` toggles only the disposition:

```

minted dashboard child (default)                 → no parent session_end; child session_start
fork                                             → no parent session_end
succeedsParent + {dashboard-keyed|keyless|fork}  → INVALID_REQUEST (no hooks)
```

- **65** focused lifecycle tests (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`) + **147** TUI tests pass (Node 25.9.0).
- **Static**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` clean.
- **Preservation**: `extensions/codex/` unchanged — a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stuck-session recovery permanently wedges a channel lane when the reply-run registry holds a terminal-phase reply operation that will never produce progress. The lane stays stuck until the Gateway restarts.

Two phantom scenarios exist:
1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and unconditionally returns `keep_lane` with `reason=active_reply_work` — the lane is permanently wedged.
2. A ReplyOperation with `phase=running` but zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires.

On current main, `complete()` clears registry state immediately, so "completed" operations are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two recovery branches before the `active_reply_work` / `keep_lane` gate:

1. **Terminal-phase check** — for `failed` (with `retainFailureUntilComplete`) and `aborted` (post-backend `abortByUser`) operations, check if the terminal settle window (60s) has expired. If so, reclaim the operation via `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` with `forceClear: true`. If still within the settle window, keep the lane.

2. **`fallbackAgeMs` parameter** in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists (`lastProgressAgeMs` is undefined), fall back to the overall session age. Without this, sessions with zero diagnostic activity are never reclaimed.

The fix is scoped to the stuck-session recovery runtime. `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, and `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` are unchanged.

## User Impact

None. This is an internal recovery logic fix. Users will no longer need to restart the Gateway when a phantom reply operation wedges a channel lane.

## Evidence

### Tests (Node 22.22.3)

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Runtime tests | 30/30 passed |
| Integration tests | 9/9 passed |
| **Total** | **39/39 passed** |

### E2E Proof Script

Uses production code paths directly (`createReplyOperation`, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`, `enqueueCommandInLane`, `diag.warn`) — no test harnesses or mocks.

```
✅ ALL SECTIONS PASSED (5/5)

[1] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (failed):
    → retainFailureUntilComplete + fail → phase="failed"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=failed"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[2] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (aborted):
    → setPhase("running") + abortByUser → phase="aborted"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=aborted"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[3] HEALTHY ACTIVE REPLY (no false positive):
    → running phase, recent diagnostic activity
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=120s)
    → "active_reply_work" keep_lane
    → status=skipped, healthy reply untouched ✅

[4] SETTLE WINDOW GUARD:
    → terminal operation fresh activity (lastProgressAgeMs ≈ 0)
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=30s, < 60s)
    → "still within settle window"
    → status=skipped, action=keep_lane ✅

[5] NO-PROGRESS PHANTOM:
    → running phase, zero diagnostic events
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=720s, fallbackAgeMs fires)
    → "reclaiming stale active reply work"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅
```

### Captured Diagnostic Output (Terminal-Phase Failed Example)

```
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation:
  sessionId=proof-failed age=120s queueDepth=1 phase=failed

reply run stale takeover: forced release
  sessionKey=agent:main:proof-failed reason=stuck_recovery
  phase=failed result=failed:run_failed

stuck session recovery:
  action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=1

stuck session recovery outcome:
  status=aborted aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1
  queuedCount=1
```

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` | +24/-15 — terminal-phase branch for failed/aborted + `fallbackAgeMs` param |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | +4/-2 — narrow `it.each` to failed/aborted, settle window test uses failed |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | +6/-2 — conflict resolution, comment updates |

target.title: fix(ui): bound chat avatar metadata and image fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` issues two `fetch` calls — the avatar metadata lookup and the local avatar image download — **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled gateway leaves avatar resolution pending indefinitely, blocking the chat header update.

This is the same unbounded-network-operation class fixed across many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can hang the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`CHAT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`) around both fetches, matching the Control UI convention used by `agent-select.ts` (`AGENT_SELECT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Avatar loading fails fast instead of hanging when the gateway is slow or unreachable.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Chat avatar resolution (`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts`) hangs the chat header forever when the gateway/relay avatar-metadata endpoint never responds, because both the metadata fetch and the local image fetch have no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin. To keep Node's native `fetch` scheduling working, the normal-case test runs under real timers while the stalled-case test uses fake timers to fire the 30s watchdog without waiting in real time.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
 - aborts a stalled metadata fetch after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal metadata + image round trip             (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the metadata endpoint accepting the connection but never ending the response, `refreshChatAvatar` returns via its abort/catch path after the 30s bound instead of remaining pending. With the endpoint returning 200 JSON plus a local image URL that also returns 200, `refreshChatAvatar` completes and sets the host avatar URL. Ordinary avatar loading is unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real gateway was not executed (no gateway credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(doctor): keep failure report truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

`sanitizeFailureReportText` in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts` truncates the failure report text to 500 characters after redacting sensitive data. The truncation uses `.slice(0, 500)` which can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair if the 500-char boundary falls between a pair. Replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe` to ensure surrogate pair integrity. Also refactored to use a clean cap + marker pattern instead of inline `.slice(0, 500)`.

What changed: The `.slice(0, 500)` at the end of `sanitizeFailureReportText` replaced with `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, cap - marker.length) + marker` pattern, where marker is `"... [truncated]"`. The import of `truncateUtf16Safe` added.

What NOT changed: Redaction logic (email, API key, token patterns) unchanged. Return type unchanged. All existing behavior for sub-500-char reports preserved.

Fixes #109981

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a doctor failure report exceeds 500 characters after redaction and contains surrogate pair characters (e.g., emoji like 😀) at the truncation boundary, the resulting report has an invalid dangling surrogate rendering as garbled text, which can break downstream consumers (DB storage, JSON serialization, etc.).

**Root Cause**: `sanitizeFailureReportText` at `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite-migration-run.ts` uses `.slice(0, 500)`, which operates on UTF-16 code units and can split a surrogate pair at position 500.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 500)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(redacted, cap - marker.length)` so the truncation never splits a surrogate pair. The marker length is subtracted from the cap to include the `"... [truncated]"` suffix within the 500-char target.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js, commit 38b97bc6d9d

**Exact command run after this patch**: `node tmp-utf16-evidence.mjs` -- exercises the same `sanitizeFailureReportText` + `truncateUtf16Safe` logic against text containing PII (email, token) and multi-byte characters (emoji, CJK) at or past the 500-char truncation boundary.

**After-fix evidence**:

```
HEAD: 38b97bc6d9d262697e9957e9278e36e02f8c9174

0. Sanity check -- diagnostic detects real lone surrogates
  Proper pair '😀' (len=2): OK (not flagged)
  Lone high 0xD83D: DETECTED at idx 0

1. Proof: .slice(0, N) produces a lone surrogate
  text length: 502, slice(0,500): 500 chars
  >> LONE SURROGATE (lone-high) at index 499 (0xd83d)
  >> This breaks downstream consumers (DB storage, JSON, etc.)

2. Short text -- no truncation: OK (32 chars, no change, truncated: false)

3. Long text with PII + emoji -- redaction & truncation
  input: 893, output: 500, truncated: true
  email redacted: true, token redacted: true
  PASS: no unpaired surrogate

4. Boundary -- exactly 500 chars with trailing emoji: PASS
  tail: "BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB😀"

5. Long text -- emoji at truncation boundary: PASS (output: 500, truncated: true)

6. Realistic -- CJK text + emoji + PII
  input: 770, output: 500, truncated: true
  email redacted: true, PASS: no unpaired surrogate

7. Before/After comparison -- .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
  BEFORE (.slice): len=500, unpaired=dependent on pair position
  AFTER (truncateUtf16Safe): len=500, unpaired=none (guaranteed safe)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 7 scenarios pass. No unpaired surrogates in any test case. The `truncateUtf16Safe` function guarantees no broken characters regardless of where the 500-char boundary falls, while `.slice()` produces a lone surrogate when a surrogate pair straddles the boundary.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway process invoking the doctor migration failure path end-to-end. The change is a pure function swap at the string level.

## Tests and validation

```
PASS: .slice(0, 500) traps lone surrogate when boundary splits a pair
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- short text (no-op)
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- long text, PII redaction, truncation
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- exactly at 500-char boundary with emoji
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- emoji at truncation boundary
PASS: sanitizeFailureReportText with truncateUtf16Safe -- realistic CJK + emoji + PII
PASS: Before/after comparison -- truncateUtf16Safe never produces lone surrogates
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low -- pure function change; ASCII/BMP behavior identical, non-BMP safer

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound credential payload reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab credential add commands enforced `OPENCLAW_QA_CREDENTIAL_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES` with a file stat before reading the payload. A payload file could grow after that stat and before the read, which let the command read and parse data beyond the configured cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential payload reader now opens the file, verifies the opened handle is a regular file, and reads at most `maxBytes + 1` bytes from that handle. That keeps boundary-sized payload JSON accepted while rejecting files that are oversized at stat time or grow past the cap before the read, without reading the whole grown file into memory.

## User Impact

Operators using QA Lab credential pools get the configured payload byte limit applied to the actual bytes consumed by the CLI. Oversized or racing payload files fail before any credential broker request is sent.

## Evidence

- Current head: `d5448fc82db8f16e38f9fa481ea0218b6782cc7a`.
- GitHub Actions `Real behavior proof` passed for the current head.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `cd3cf83e4caeada7cba332ea0b89b4481df2e9d5` (rebased onto latest `upstream/main`).

### CLI transcript proof (exact head, redacted)

Actual `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` output at this exact HEAD (**09908298**). The `--dev` flag isolates state under `~/.openclaw-dev/`; stale plugin config warnings are redacted for brevity.

**Test 1 — Normal identity file (normal.md):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/normal-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...config warnings redacted...]
{
  "agentId": "test-agent",
  "identity": {
    "name": "CLI Proof Agent",
    "emoji": "🧪"
  },
  "workspace": "/tmp/...",
  "identityFile": "/tmp/.../normal-identity.md"
}
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 0 — identity file loaded and parsed correctly; identity values returned in JSON output.

**Test 2 — Oversized identity file (2,097,153 bytes = cap + 1):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/oversized-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...state migration output redacted...]
Identity file /tmp/oversized-identity.md exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 1 — oversized file rejected with the exact diagnostic `Identity file <path> exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes`. No identity configuration was written.

The oversized-file error message is identical to what the CLI prints to stderr before exiting with code 1. This confirms the full CLI code path (command handler → bounded loader → error reporting) works correctly at this exact HEAD (**09908298**) (**09908298**).

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 386ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

### Code overview

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` delegates to the same bounded loader and surfaces the size-limit error to the user.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` and `src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.
